newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU attaches conditions to D.Telekom tariffs plan.
newsitem.headline: EU attaches conditions to D.Telekom tariffs plan.

text.p: The European Commission said on Thursday Deutsche Telekom's plan to grant price discounts to big customers could go ahead as planned on November 1 but only under conditions.

A statement said European Union Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert had agreed that the German Federal Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications (BMPT) grant Deutsche Telekom's (DT) application for "certain new business customer tariffs by 1 November 1996".

"His agreement is conditional on the conclusion of retroactive network access agreements between DT and its competitors by 31 December 1996 and on the BMPT taking additional regulatory steps required for competitive network access in the German market before that date," it said.
Van Miert warned the EU executive would act swiftly if Deutsche Telecom's competitors were denied network access on fair terms by the December 31 deadline.
The move is designed to ensure that business rivals can compete effectively with Deutsche Telekom in Germany -- Europe's largest telecoms market.

But although the conditions will further dent Telekom's dominant position in the German market, they are not of a nature to upset its sell-off on November 18 in the largest-ever initial public offering operation.

In practice, the Commission's decision will allow Deutsche Telekom to go ahead with discounts of up to 35 percent to large business clients on Friday as planned while imposing conditions likely to benefit rival telecoms operators from the same date.

The conditions will address the issue of newcomers' right to interconnect with the established infrastructure network of Deutsche Telekom -- a highly thorny problem in all national telecoms markets previously controlled by a monopoly.
In a related issue, the Commission will also deal with "break-in and break-out access conditions" to Telekom's infrastructure and business networks in particular.
British Telecommunications Plc welcomed the additional conditions, but said it would have been better to delay the plan altogether.
"We are extremely concerned about the issue of timing," Larry Stone, BT's head of European Union affairs, told Reuters.
"This is because if Deutsche Telekom is allowed to go ahead with the tariffs it will tie in customers before its competitors have the chance to compete for them," Stone said.
"(It would have been better) not to allow this tariff to proceed at all until such time as the conditions are up and running," he added.

Deutsche Telekom's main rivals in Germany argued to the Commission earlier this month that the tariff discounts ought to be delayed because the conditions meant to prevent it from abusing its dominant position had not been fulfilled.
The Commission cleared the discounts in June provided the German government granted new telecoms licences and promoted negotiations on access to Telekom's infrastructure.
To ensure that fair competition did not remain a empty concept, the Commission would be asking Germany to make regulatory changes before the end of the year that would be retroactive.

"Before December 31 1996 the BMPT shall allot special network access numbers to applicants and change current regulations allowing DT to charge third-party network operators by the second," the Commission said.

The companies that have complained to the Commission about Telekom's new pricing policy include Communications Network International, the Mannesmann unit, Thyssen subsidiary Plus Net, WorldCom Inc and Viag Interkom, the joint venture of Viag AG and British Telecommunications Plc .
Van Miert and German Post and Telecommunications Minister Wolfgang Boetsch have been in constant contact in the past weeks to defuse a crisis that could damage Deutsche Telekom's privatisation.
